decisive_items: struck by lightning directly to the right forehead while hiking
central macular thickening in fundus examination
Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption in the right eye
response.rationale: R5 best integrates the lightning trauma with the macular OCT/fundus evidence, including central thickening, cystoid changes, and subfoveal ellipsoid disruption. R2 captures only the photoreceptor/outer-retinal component without the traumatic cause or cystoid phase, while R1, R3, and R4 each reflect only part of the picture: transient CME, late cataract, or mechanism alone.

rejected.why: Only the transient intraretinal cystoid component; initial OCT showed no cystoid changes and later cystoid decreased, so it is not the unifying diagnosis.
Late, mild posterior subcapsular cataract; initial anterior segment was normal, and it does not explain early visual loss or macular OCT findings.
Raw support is limited to the lightning strike mechanism, with no raw ocular finding; too broad/under-specified as the diagnosis.
